items.title: Live: Donald Trump says he's not ready to make a deal with Iran because 'terms aren't good enough'
items.description: The US president renews his call for other nations to help secure the Strait of Hormuz as the Iran war rages on, threatening further strikes on the Kharg Island oil export hub.

items.title: 'Almost unhinged': UAE minister tells ABC 'Iran attacks were a surprise'
items.description: Iran's actions in attacking neighbouring countries were unprecedented, "almost unhinged" and irrational, according to a senior United Arab Emirates minister.

items.title: The world feels like it's out of control. Could this chaos be deliberate?
items.description: Around the world, things are moving at a dizzying speed, and the pace is being set from Washington. Some people claim this is a deliberate strategy to overwhelm us, and that it comes with consequences.

items.title: 'I'm worried about them': Three members of Iranian women's team return home after seeking asylum
items.description: Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke confirms that a trio of members of the Iranian women's football team, who were given humanitarian visas, chose to return home.

items.title: Live: Piastri fails to start again as McLaren suffer double blow in China
items.description: Oscar Piastri has not started either of the opening two grands prix of the 2026 Formula 1 season, as McLaren suffered a double-blow in China. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Demons hang on to beat Saints in thriller as Suns host Eagles
items.description: The Demons mark new coach Steven King's first match in charge with a gripping 13-point win over the Saints, while the Suns meet the Eagles on the Gold Coast. Follow live.

items.title: Pilot's body located after helicopter crash in 'dense bushland'
items.description: NSW Police say the body located after a helicopter crash in north-east NSW is yet to be identified, but they believe it's the 77-year-old pilot.

items.title: 18yo dies, another critically injured after falling from Mount Beerwah
items.description: An 18-year-old woman has died and an 18-year-old man has been critically injured after falling while climbing Mount Beerwah in the Glasshouse Mountains on Queensland's Sunshine Coast.

items.title: Cracks showing in concrete tomb tasked with containing nuclear problem
items.description: Cracks have appeared in a concrete dome holding 120,000 tonnes of contaminated soil and debris from Cold War-era nuclear bomb tests.

items.title: Live: 'Half their salary cap gone': Knights costly win over Manly
items.description: Kalyn Ponga and Dylan Brown are both forced from the field in the first half as the Newcastle Knights ran riot against the Sea Eagles at Brookvale Oval. Follow live.

items.title: Former NRL star Chris Walker arrested on Gold Coast in alleged DV case
items.description: Former Queensland State of Origin player Chris Walker has been arrested on the Gold Coast in relation to alleged domestic violence offences, Queensland Police have confirmed.

items.title: Danish royals King Frederik and Queen Mary get rare treat at Uluru
items.description: Queen Mary and King Frederik of Denmark have begun the second day of their royal visit to Australia after waking in the red desert sand of Uluru in Central Australia.

items.title: Iran targets big tech and AI with strikes on data centres
items.description: Iran struck three data centres in the Middle East, and has signalled that technology infrastructure will continue to be in the firing line.

items.title: Is he 'on the run' or 'disfigured'? Mystery surrounds Iran's new supreme leader
items.description: Late last week, Iran's new supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, broke his silence after days of intensifying rumours about his health and whereabouts, but it did little to put them to rest.

items.title: Why Yothu Yindi’s 'black Elvis' turned his back on a wild rockstar life
items.description: Rockstar. Leader. Peacemaker. Witiyana Marika was riding the wave of international fame in the band Yothu Yindi when his dying father called him back to Arnhem Land.

items.title: Motörhead guitarist Phil Campbell dies aged 64
items.description: In a statement on Instagram, his family says he "passed away peacefully following a long and courageous battle in intensive care after a complex major operation".

items.title: Lainey Wilson is everywhere — here's how she pulls it off
items.description: Arena tours, feature films and a new single — here's how one of America's biggest stars keeps climbing.

items.title: Fuel runs out in two north-west Victorian towns
items.description: Robinvale, located about 70 kilometres east from Mildura, ran out of fuel on Saturday evening, while Hattah, to Mildura's south, hit empty on Sunday.

items.title: Body of swimmer found at NSW south coast beach
items.description: Authorities have located the body of a swimmer, a man believed to have been aged in his 20s, at Werri Beach on the NSW south coast.

items.title: A backpacker who killed a Tasmanian sex worker now runs a cafe in Germany
items.description: In 2020, a German backpacker strangled a Tasmanian sex worker, then fled with her mobile phone and cash. His version of events was accepted by an Australian court, which jailed him for manslaughter. Now, German authorities are re-examining the case.

items.title: Green records 'nerve-racking' Australian Open win to end 12-year drought
items.description: Hannah Green says her nerves were frayed during her one-stroke victory at the Women's Australian Open in Adelaide.

items.title: Inside a family's 'exhausting' battle with the NDIS to support disabled son
items.description: The parents of a disabled teenager have lifted the lid on the toll lobbying the NDIS for adequate support has taken on their lives, saying they feel exhausted and let down.

items.title: Lynelle thought her adoption was genuine. Then she applied for a licence
items.description: Adoptees who were brought to Australia from overseas — some in murky circumstances — call on the Commonwealth to broaden an inquiry launched this week.

items.title: 'They honestly saved my life': The bikers helping abused kids feel safe
items.description: BACA members accompany kids to court, stand guard outside their homes, and provide a sense of safety with burly presences and deeply rumbling motorbikes.

items.title: Why some women experience intense negative feelings while breastfeeding
items.description: Anger, dread, anxiety, guilt, worry and disconnect are just some of the feelings described by women who experience breastfeeding aversion response.
